seeds.text: When it rains here, the drops rattle like glass beads.
The malevolent spirit is only a child who got lost.
A rival adventuring party is already there.
Fear: the villain is fleeing something too.
A horn every dog within a mile obeys.

concept.title: The Mayor’s Chain
concept.tagline: Break into Njal’s strongroom in Crowfell, take the chain of office and the pawn note, and get away before the buyer arrives at dawn.
concept.teaser: Svend comes to the heroes in secret with a sketch of Njal’s house and a plea: bring back the chain and the pawn note before dawn, and no one need ever know.
concept.premise: In the hungry spring, Svend, the mayor of Lowmoor, secretly pawned the town’s chain of office to Njal to buy grain, and Njal made sure the shop was shut on the day Svend came to redeem it. Now Njal, who has never forgiven Svend for keeping Njal off the council, has sold the chain to a foreign buyer who collects it at dawn, and the same morning Njal means to read the pawn note aloud in the square. The chain lies in Njal’s strongroom in Crowfell, guarded by bandits, a clever lock and a household that never sleeps.
concept.goal: Break into Njal’s strongroom in Crowfell, take the chain of office and the pawn note, and get away before the buyer arrives at dawn.

objective.target: The town’s chain of office and Svend’s pawn note
objective.state: In an iron chest in the strongroom beneath Njal’s bedchamber; the chest has two locks, and the key to one hangs round Njal’s neck. The bandit captain keeps watch in the passage outside.
objective.resolution: Get in, open both locks and come out with the chain and the note without waking Njal, or at least before the buyer arrives. If the alarm is raised, the escape becomes a chase, and Njal will claim the chain was stolen from an honest pawnbroker. By force: defeat the bandit captain and the others or break through (a DC 16 Strength (Athletics) check; a door or chain has AC 15 and 18 HP). On a failure, 10 minutes pass and the noise wakes the rest of the place. Without a fight: persuade or bribe whoever guards the objective (a DC 13 Charisma (Persuasion) check, or 150 gp), or sneak past (a DC 13 Dexterity (Stealth) check for the whole group). On a failure, someone raises the alarm and Njal gets a round to prepare.

concept.stakes: If the chain leaves town at dawn, Lowmoor’s honour is sold to strangers, Svend is driven from office, and Njal has shown the whole town what it costs to stand in Njal’s way.

clock.start: Evening. Svend has told the heroes everything and given them a sketch of the house; the buyer is expected at dawn, nine hours from now.

ticks.when: After 1 hour (when the bell strikes ten)
ticks.event: Njal drinks the sleeping draught and sleeps like a stone for the next five hours.
ticks.sign: The light in Njal’s bedchamber goes out, and Ylva sets an empty cup out on the stair.

ticks.when: After 6 hours (7 if Ylva made the draught stronger)
ticks.event: The draught wears off, and Njal gets up to look at the chain one last time.
ticks.sign: Light in the bedchamber again, and the sound of a heavy door opening beneath the house.

ticks.event: The buyer arrives with armed companions, pays and rides off with the chain.
ticks.sign: Hooves at Crowfell, and Njal standing in the doorway, smiling.

clock.deadline: After 9 hours, at dawn, it is too late: the chain is sold and on its way abroad, and the pawn note is read aloud in the square.
clock.costs: The scenes give the travel times, the shortcuts and how long a thorough search takes. A short rest takes 1 hour.

hooks: Svend comes to the heroes in secret with a sketch of Njal’s house and a plea: bring back the chain and the pawn note before dawn, and no one need ever know.
A learned friend of the wizard writes from Lowmoor that Svend needs a clever mind and that the matter cannot wait.
The temple sends the cleric to Lowmoor: Svend has asked for help, and the people there need someone who is neither afraid nor bought.

villain.name: Njal
villain.nature: A pawnbroker with an old grudge against the mayor
villain.want: To see Svend humiliated before all of Lowmoor, and to be the one who exposed the mayor’s secret.
villain.plan: First, Njal shut the shop on the day the pledge was due, so the chain fell lawfully to Njal. Then Njal sold it to a buyer from abroad who collects it at dawn, though before dawn Njal cannot resist going down to look at it one last time. The same morning Njal reads the pawn note aloud in the square, and Svend must resign in shame.
villain.weakness: Njal sleeps lightly and takes a sleeping draught every night when the bell strikes ten, because the fear of thieves keeps Njal awake. Ylva, the house servant, mixes the draught and has good reason to hate Njal.

cast.name: Svend
cast.role: A mayor who pawned the town’s chain to buy grain

cast.name: Ylva
cast.role: A servant in Njal’s house who mixes Njal’s sleeping draught

outline.title: The Mayor’s Confession
outline.purpose: Svend, the mayor of Lowmoor, has sought the heroes out in secret and brought them into the empty council chamber. Here Svend confesses that the town’s chain of office was pawned to Njal in the hungry spring to buy grain, that Njal cheated Svend out of redeeming it, and that a foreign buyer collects it at dawn. Svend gives the heroes a sketch of Njal’s house and begs them to bring back both the chain and the pawn note, so that no one need ever know.

outline.title: The Sleeping Draught
outline.purpose: Before the bell strikes ten, Ylva, the servant in Njal’s house, stands at the herbalist’s counter buying herbs for the sleeping draught Ylva mixes for Njal. Ylva hates Njal and can make the draught stronger, leave the kitchen door unbarred or explain how the household sleeps, if the heroes get there in time and can be trusted.

outline.title: The Pledge Book
outline.purpose: Njal’s pawnshop in Lowmoor stands dark for the night, and the pledge book inside shows that the redemption day for pledge no. 113 has been corrected in fresher ink. In the drawer lies a copy of the bill of sale to the buyer. Across the lane lives the mason who built the strongroom and will gladly sell the plan of it for a good price.

outline.title: The Office Clock
outline.purpose: The heroes cross the yard between the rounds of Njal’s bandits and slip into the office, where the panel hides the stair down and the tall clock hides the key to one of the locks. The patrols keep away from the passage below, where only the bandit captain goes, so up here the danger is being seen; down there it is the bandit captain, and if there is noise in the passage, the patrols arrive within two rounds.

outline.title: The Iron Chest
outline.purpose: Beneath Njal’s bedchamber lies the strongroom, where the chain and the pawn note rest in an iron chest bolted to the floor, with two locks; the bandit captain keeps watch in the passage outside and serves Njal, like the patrols. Before dawn Njal cannot resist going down to look at the chain one last time, with a lamp and the key around their neck: after 6 hours (7 if Ylva made the draught stronger), or sooner if a fight or noise at the chest carries up through the floor. The heroes must open both locks and get out with the chain and the note before the buyer arrives.

outline.title: The Aftermath
outline.purpose: The chain is back in the town hall before dawn, the buyer leaves empty-handed, and the pawn note burns in Svend’s fireplace. Njal cannot report the theft without revealing the fraud in the pledge book, but Njal knows who was there and will not forget it.

clues.observation: In the shop drawer under the pledge book lies a copy of the bill of sale to the buyer from abroad, signed by Njal.
clues.inference: Njal sold the chain knowing that it belongs to the town.
clues.handout:
Sold: one gold chain of office, 14 links, with the town arms.
To be collected at dawn at Crowfell. The seller warrants that no one in Lowmoor has any claim on it.
— Njal

clues.observation: The neighbours remember that Njal’s shop was shut on the very day Svend came with the money, for the first time in twenty years.
clues.inference: Njal kept the shop shut on purpose.

clues.observation: The pledge book in Njal’s shop has been corrected in fresher ink: the redemption day has been moved a day earlier.
clues.inference: Njal cheated Svend out of the redemption and so has no right to the chain.
clues.handout:
Pledge no. 113: chain of office, gold, 14 links. Pledged by Svend.
To be redeemed by: 9th (corrected to 8th) day of the sowing month.
Not redeemed. Falls to the pawnbroker.

clues.observation: The mason who built the strongroom still has the plan and will gladly sell it for a good price.
clues.inference: The way in is through the office, and the second key is hidden in the office clock.
clues.handout:
Strongroom under the bedchamber. Access by the stair behind the panel in the office.
Air shaft from the yard, a hand wide, two ells long.
Chest bolted to the floor. Two locks: one key for the owner, one in the office clock.

clues.observation: Whenever Njal has been to the strongroom, a faint smell of lamp oil and iron hangs by the panel in the office, and the floor in front of it is worn smooth.
clues.inference: The panel in the office is the door down to the strongroom.

clues.observation: Ylva, the house servant, says that Njal drinks a sleeping draught every night when the bell strikes ten, and that Ylva is the one who mixes it.
clues.inference: For five hours after ten, Njal sleeps like a stone, and Ylva might be persuaded to make the draught stronger.

partyMoments.moment: The key comes free without stopping the pendulum, and the clock ticks on as if nothing had happened (scene 4, “The Office Clock”: Dexterity (Sleight of Hand), DC 13).
Svend is ashamed but speaks the truth: the grain saved the town (scene 1, “The Mayor’s Confession”: Wisdom (Insight), DC 10).
The climax (scene 5, “The Iron Chest”): the right spell at the right moment.
Njal hands over the key and promises silence: Njal cannot report the theft without revealing the fraud, and knows it (scene 5, “The Iron Chest”: Charisma (Intimidation), DC 13).

scenes.title: The Mayor’s Confession
scenes.summary: Svend, the mayor of Lowmoor, has sought the heroes out in secret and brought them into the empty council chamber. Here Svend confesses that the town’s chain of office was pawned to Njal in the hungry spring to buy grain, that Njal cheated Svend out of redeeming it, and that a foreign buyer collects it at dawn. Svend gives the heroes a sketch of Njal’s house and begs them to bring back both the chain and the pawn note, so that no one need ever know.
scenes.readAloud: The council chamber is dark except for a single lamp on the long table. On the wall behind the mayor’s chair hangs the town’s painted coat of arms, and beneath it an iron hook with nothing on it. From the square outside come footsteps, drawing closer, then passing by.
details: The sketch shows the yard, the office and the bedchamber, but not the strongroom, which Svend has never seen. Svend remembers that the shop was shut on the very day Svend came with the money, for the first time in twenty years, and the neighbours remember it too.
The town crier is drinking at the inn across from the town hall, boasting that Njal has paid extra for "big news about the mayor" in the square tomorrow morning.
Njal has hated Svend ever since Svend kept Njal off the council. No one may know: Svend can use neither the watch nor the council, only the heroes.

checks.success: Svend is ashamed but speaks the truth: the grain saved the town. Pressed, Svend mentions that Ylva, a servant in Njal’s house, once asked for help, and that Ylva fetches herbs for Njal’s sleeping draught from the herbalist every evening.
checks.failure: Svend only remembers Ylva’s name as the heroes are on their way out. They reach Ylva with only minutes to spare before the bell strikes ten.

checks.success: Svend opens the town chest: enough silver to buy the mason’s plan and bribe whoever needs bribing.
checks.failure: Svend has nothing more to give than the sketch and a promise. The heroes must pay the mason and everyone else themselves.

alternatives: Head straight for Njal’s house with only the sketch: it is quick, but the sketch shows neither the strongroom nor the second key.
Have Svend confess in the square at dawn, before Njal can: the pawn note loses its sting, but the chain must still be recovered.
scenes.dmNotes: Make Svend sympathetic: the chain was pawned to give the town bread, not to make anyone rich. The players should feel they are stealing back the town’s honour, not just a trinket.

scenes.title: The Sleeping Draught
scenes.summary: Before the bell strikes ten, Ylva, the servant in Njal’s house, stands at the herbalist’s counter buying herbs for the sleeping draught Ylva mixes for Njal. Ylva hates Njal and can make the draught stronger, leave the kitchen door unbarred or explain how the household sleeps, if the heroes get there in time and can be trusted.
scenes.readAloud: The herbalist’s shop is narrow and smells of camphor and dried flowers. A servant in a grey apron counts out coins for a small paper twist of herbs, glancing at the door each time it opens. From the tower the bell strikes the three-quarter hour.
details: Njal drinks the draught when the bell strikes ten and sleeps like a stone for five hours. Ylva can make it stronger, so that Njal sleeps an hour longer, but will not give Njal anything that could kill.
Ylva hates Njal with good reason: Njal has held Ylva’s mother’s ring in pawn for three years and takes the interest out of Ylva’s wages. The ring lies in the strongroom with a numbered tag.

Ylva knows that Njal’s bandits walk rounds of the house, that the bandit captain keeps to the passage below, and that Njal sleeps with a key on a cord around their neck. After ten Ylva is back in the house and sets an empty cup out on the stair once Njal is asleep.

checks.success: Ylva agrees to make the draught stronger and leave the kitchen door unbarred. Njal wakes only after 7 hours instead of 6.
checks.failure: Ylva dares not touch the draught but promises to leave the kitchen door unbarred. The clock runs as before.

checks.success: The heroes see that Ylva’s hatred is real and that Ylva would rather lose their position than betray them. A promise to get Ylva’s mother’s ring back binds Ylva to the plan.
checks.failure: The heroes are unsure of Ylva and say too much or too little. Ylva helps, but is so nervous that the other servants in the house notice.

alternatives: If the heroes reach the herbalist too late, they can watch the stair from the street: the empty cup tells them Njal is asleep.
Buy Ylva out: enough money to leave town tomorrow is a better promise than revenge.
scenes.dmNotes: Use a real clock: the bell strikes ten once the scene has run a set time, and then Ylva is gone. Ylva’s fear is the scene; one wrong word and Ylva hurries out of the door.

scenes.title: The Pledge Book
scenes.summary: Njal’s pawnshop in Lowmoor stands dark for the night, and the pledge book inside shows that the redemption day for pledge no. 113 has been corrected in fresher ink. In the drawer lies a copy of the bill of sale to the buyer. Across the lane lives the mason who built the strongroom and will gladly sell the plan of it for a good price.
scenes.readAloud: The pawnshop’s shutters are closed and locked, and a sign in the window says "Shut" in neat letters. Through a crack between the boards, moonlight falls on shelves of other people’s things: boots, a fiddle, a cradle. Across the lane a light still burns in a workshop full of stone dust and chisels.
details: In the pledge book, the redemption day for pledge no. 113 has been changed from the 9th to the 8th in fresher ink than the rest of the page. It is the proof that Njal cheated Svend.

In the drawer under the counter lies the copy of the bill of sale: the chain is to be collected at dawn at Crowfell, and Njal warrants that no one in Lowmoor has any claim on it. The shop’s lock is simple, but the watchman passes every quarter of an hour.

The mason remembers that the shop was shut on the day the mayor came with the money, and still has the plan of the strongroom: the stair behind the panel in the office, the air shaft from the yard, the chest with two locks and the key in the office clock.

checks.success: The heroes are in and out between the watchman’s rounds, and nobody knows the pledge book has been opened.
checks.failure: The watchman sees a light in the shop and starts asking questions. The heroes lose half an hour talking their way out, or Svend’s name settles it, but then the watchman knows the mayor is involved.

checks.success: The mason sells the plan at a fair price and adds that the key in the clock hangs behind the pendulum.
checks.failure: The mason wants more than the heroes have. They can pay with a promise from Svend, but the haggling costs half an hour.

alternatives: Skip the plan: the smell at the panel and the worn floor show the way down, but the heroes must then search the office for the second key.
Take the pledge book along: if the heroes end up face to face with Njal in the strongroom, it is a better weapon than any sword.
scenes.dmNotes: This is where the players plan: give them the mason’s plan as a real piece of paper and let them argue over it. Write their plan down so you know where it can go wrong.

scenes.title: The Office Clock
scenes.summary: The heroes cross the yard between the rounds of Njal’s bandits and slip into the office, where the panel hides the stair down and the tall clock hides the key to one of the locks. The patrols keep away from the passage below, where only the bandit captain goes, so up here the danger is being seen; down there it is the bandit captain, and if there is noise in the passage, the patrols arrive within two rounds.
scenes.readAloud: The yard is paved and swept clean, and a lantern hangs over the kitchen door. Footsteps cross the yard and fade round the corner of the house; a little later they come back. Inside the office a tall clock ticks beside a dark wooden panel, and the floor in front of the panel is worn smooth.
details: Njal’s bandits walk rounds of the house in pairs and keep away from the passage outside the strongroom. Before ten Njal is awake; once the light in the bedchamber goes out and Ylva sets an empty cup on the stair, Njal is asleep.
A faint smell of lamp oil and iron hangs by the panel, and the floor before it is worn smooth. Behind the panel a narrow stair goes down to the passage where the bandit captain keeps watch.
The key to one lock hangs behind the clock’s pendulum. If the pendulum stops, the clock stops ticking, and that silence is the first thing Njal notices when coming through the office after 6 hours.

checks.success: The heroes cross the yard in the gap between two rounds and are in the office without a sound.
checks.failure: A patrol glimpses a shadow and comes to look. The heroes must hide or fight, and the fight must be quiet, or the household wakes.

checks.success: The key comes free without stopping the pendulum, and the clock ticks on as if nothing had happened.
checks.failure: The pendulum stops and the clock falls silent. When Njal comes through the office after 6 hours (7 if Ylva made the draught stronger), Njal hears the silence and goes down shouting for the bandit captain.

alternatives: If Ylva left the kitchen door unbarred, the heroes can go in through the house instead of across the open yard.
Have one hero keep watch in the yard and signal at every round while the others work in the office.
scenes.dmNotes: Make the patrol pattern visible: describe it twice so the players can time it. A plan that works because the players paid attention is the whole joy of a heist.

scenes.title: The Iron Chest
scenes.summary: Beneath Njal’s bedchamber lies the strongroom, where the chain and the pawn note rest in an iron chest bolted to the floor, with two locks; the bandit captain keeps watch in the passage outside and serves Njal, like the patrols. Before dawn Njal cannot resist going down to look at the chain one last time, with a lamp and the key around their neck: after 6 hours (7 if Ylva made the draught stronger), or sooner if a fight or noise at the chest carries up through the floor. The heroes must open both locks and get out with the chain and the note before the buyer arrives.
scenes.readAloud: The stair behind the panel smells of lamp oil and iron and ends in a short stone passage where someone or something shifts in the dark before a heavy, iron-bound door. Beyond the door lies a low room with shelves full of pledges: candlesticks, silver cups and a christening cup, each with its numbered tag. In the middle of the floor stands an iron chest with two keyholes, bolted to the stone.
details: If Njal is here, Njal does not fight (stat block: noble). Should the fight go badly, Njal tries to bargain or flee and, if cornered, would rather surrender than die.
One lock opens with the key from the office clock, the other with the key round Njal’s neck. The heroes can lift it from the sleeping Njal, take it when Njal comes down, or pick the lock.

After 6 hours (7 if Ylva made the draught stronger), or when noise from a fight or the chest wakes Njal, Njal comes down the stair in nightclothes with a lamp, threatening to cry thief and claiming to be an honest pawnbroker, but is afraid and would rather bargain than be hurt.

In the chest lie the chain, wrapped in velvet, and the pawn note with Svend’s signature. If the heroes are gone before Njal wakes (6 hours, 7 with the stronger draught), Njal finds the chest empty and cannot report the theft without revealing the fraud in the pledge book.
On the strongroom’s shelves of pledges lies one more thing: a horn every dog within a mile obeys.

checks.success: The second lock gives with a small click, and the chest opens without a sound.
checks.failure: The pick snaps in the lock with a sharp crack that carries up through the floor. Njal wakes, and the bandit captain comes to the door.

checks.success: Njal hands over the key and promises silence: Njal cannot report the theft without revealing the fraud, and knows it.
checks.failure: Njal screams for the household. The escape becomes a chase through the house, and Njal will claim the chain was stolen from an honest pawnbroker.

alternatives: Lay the corrected page of the pledge book before Njal: if the theft is reported, the fraud comes out, and Njal lets the heroes go.
Wait in the dark strongroom until Njal comes down with the key after 6 hours (7 if Ylva made the draught stronger), and take it at the door.
scenes.dmNotes: Let the room tell the story: every shelf holds someone else’s treasure, and one of the tags belongs to Ylva’s mother’s ring. Let Njal’s first words be a lie about honesty, and let the heroes answer with the pledge book.

scenes.title: The Aftermath
scenes.summary: The chain is back in the town hall before dawn, the buyer leaves empty-handed, and the pawn note burns in Svend’s fireplace. Njal cannot report the theft without revealing the fraud in the pledge book, but Njal knows who was there and will not forget it.
scenes.readAloud: At dawn people gather in the square of Lowmoor, for rumour says something is to be read aloud. From the town hall steps the buyer’s carriage can be seen waiting at Njal’s gate with the horses in harness.
details: If the heroes only partly succeed: The heroes get the chain out, but the pawn note stays behind, and at dawn Njal reads it aloud in the square. The town keeps its chain, but Svend must resign, and Njal is voted onto the council to fill the empty seat.

If the heroes fail: At dawn the buyer rides away with the chain, and Njal reads the pawn note aloud to a gaping square. Svend is driven from office, Njal takes a seat on the council, and somewhere far away Lowmoor’s chain now hangs in a foreign collector’s cabinet.
scenes.dmNotes: Narrate the ending that matches what the heroes actually achieved: if they succeeded, the summary holds; if not, one of the other two endings does. Then let each player say what their hero does next.

locations.name: The Office Clock

encounter.tactics: The strongest leads and the others follow. They come in two waves: 3 at once and 3 at the end of the second round. They fight while they outnumber the heroes and fall back once half of them are down.

locations.name: The Scriptorium of Dried Ink
locations.readAloud: The sconces hold fresh torches that have never been lit. A clock ticks somewhere, unevenly, like the steps of someone with a limp.
locations.description: A board game sits mid-match; moving the black queen slides out a drawer beneath the tabletop.
features: A hoist with a basket hangs in a shaft, and the rope holds one person at a time.
A row of small bells hangs from the ceiling on thin cords, and the slightest touch sets them all ringing.
locations.secret: The passage carries voices from a room further in, and anyone standing in the corner can hear everything said in there.

locations.name: The Iron Chest
locations.readAloud: The stair behind the panel smells of lamp oil and iron and ends in a short stone passage where someone or something shifts in the dark before a heavy, iron-bound door. encounter.tactics: The bandit captain stands guard alone in the passage and leads the attack on the nearest hero. If the fight is heard, the six bandits of the patrols arrive within two rounds and join in; bandits the heroes have already beaten in the yard do not come. Njal does not fight, keeps out of the way and tries to bargain once the fight turns.

treasure: A horn every dog within a mile obeys.

npcs.name: Njal
npcs.look: Wears armour polished so bright that others can see themselves in it.
npcs.personality: Dutiful to the point of absurdity.
npcs.wants: To see Svend humiliated before all of Lowmoor, and to be the one who exposed the mayor’s secret.
npcs.secret: Njal sleeps lightly and takes a sleeping draught every night when the bell strikes ten, because the fear of thieves keeps Njal awake. Ylva, the house servant, mixes the draught and has good reason to hate Njal.
npcs.voice: Always asks for names a second time and repeats them wrong.

npcs.name: Svend
npcs.role: A mayor who pawned the town’s chain to buy grain
npcs.look: Is unusually tall and always stoops as if the ceiling were too low, even outdoors.
npcs.personality: Vengeful, with a long list and a longer memory.
npcs.wants: Wants the chain back in the town hall before anyone discovers it was ever gone.
npcs.secret: Kept Njal off the council years ago with a rumour that was not true, and knows full well the grudge is not without cause.

npcs.name: Ylva
npcs.role: A servant in Njal’s house who mixes Njal’s sleeping draught
npcs.look: Wears a cloak stitched together from old flags.
npcs.personality: Cheerful despite everything, almost infuriatingly so.
npcs.wants: Wants the year’s wages Njal owes, and a position in another household.
npcs.secret: Has pilfered small things from Njal for years and is afraid a break-in will bring it all to light.
npcs.voice: Speaks as if reading aloud from a document, and keeps adjusting their spectacles.

rewards.name: A topaz that was once the eye of a statue
A gold brooch shaped like a bee, worn by three generations of beekeepers
The Homeward Thread
rewards.description: A spool of red yarn. Tie one end to a door; the thread unrolls for up to a mile, and only the one who tied it can see it.

rewards.name: A horn every dog within a mile obeys
rewards.description: The real treasure of the adventure. It is worth more to the right people than to any merchant.

endings.success: The chain is back in the town hall before dawn, the buyer leaves empty-handed, and the pawn note burns in Svend’s fireplace. Njal cannot report the theft without revealing the fraud in the pledge book, but Njal knows who was there and will not forget it.
endings.partial: The heroes get the chain out, but the pawn note stays behind, and at dawn Njal reads it aloud in the square. The town keeps its chain, but Svend must resign, and Njal is voted onto the council to fill the empty seat.
endings.failure: At dawn the buyer rides away with the chain, and Njal reads the pawn note aloud to a gaping square. Svend is driven from office, Njal takes a seat on the council, and somewhere far away Lowmoor’s chain now hangs in a foreign collector’s cabinet.

unexpected.trigger: The heroes set the place on fire.
unexpected.response: Let it burn, but put something important at risk: a captive, the evidence or the treasure. The fire becomes a scene of its own.

unexpected.trigger: The heroes use magic to skip a whole part of the adventure.
unexpected.response: Reward the clever move, but give it a price: they arrive without their gear, at the wrong moment, or something has noticed the magic.

unexpected.trigger: The players ask something you have no answer for.
unexpected.response: Ask back: "What do you think?" Use the best answer, or have a minor character guess wrong while you think.

unexpected.trigger: The heroes try to buy their way out of trouble.
unexpected.response: Let the money work once, and let the price rise the next time. Anyone who takes a bribe can sell the heroes on, too.

unexpected.trigger: The heroes miss a vital clue.
unexpected.response: Move the clue: let it turn up somewhere else in a new form, or have a minor character bring it. A mystery must never stall on a single roll.

tips: Tell the players about a trap once they have found it, and let them work out how to get past.
Write the clock’s steps on a card and show the players when it moves. Visible time builds tension.
Raise or lower the number of foes as you go; what the players have not seen can still change.
Let victory cost something. A scar, a loss or a hard choice makes it worth more.
sequelHooks: Something from Crowfell has followed one of the heroes home, and it is slowly waking.
A new bridge that nobody built now stands across the road home.
